Truckbase · order creation → invoicing

Exploratory Findings

Lead QA Engineer take-home · Part 2

Findings3
ScopeOrder → Invoice
Severity2 Critical, 1 Med
RecommendationDo not ship

Three findings from exploratory testing of the order creation to Truckbase invoicing path, reproduced against Orders #14 and #15. Observations that fell outside the assigned workflow, or below the threshold for a finding, are listed at the end. Testing was time-boxed and covered a single customer, a flat rate, and two stops.

Finding 01

No validation on the linehaul rate; negative values generate a billable invoice

Critical

Reproduction

StepExpectedActual
1Enter 0-1234.56 in the simple Linehaul rate field Field rejects non-numeric input with a visible error Accepted silently; summary bar shows “-”
2Open Show advanced rates, enter -1234.56 Negative value rejected Accepted; line total computes to -$1,234.56
3Add two stops and save the order Save blocked while the rate is invalid Order saves with Total rate -$1,234.56
4Create a Truckbase invoice from the order overlay Invoice creation blocked Dialog opens carrying -$1,234.56
5Preview the invoice — PDF renders TOTAL DUE: -$1,234.56

Business impact

A negative invoice is effectively an unintended credit memo. If sent, the customer receives a document requesting negative payment — at best confusing, at worst treated as a credit against amounts owed. If invoices sync to accounting, the carrier's receivables are wrong.

The failure is entirely silent: no warning, no error, and no visual distinction from a correct invoice. That is what makes it expensive. An invoice that fails to generate is noticed immediately; one that generates with the wrong sign may not surface until reconciliation.

Evidence

Recommended follow-up

Validation belongs in three places: client-side for immediate feedback, server-side for enforcement, and a sanity check at invoice generation so a bad value cannot reach a customer-facing document even if earlier layers are bypassed. Worth checking whether other monetary fields — expenses, fuel, accessorials — share the same gap, and whether a negative invoice would sync to QuickBooks.

Finding 02

Invoice cannot be viewed from the invoices list, or sent to the customer

Critical

Reproduction

StepExpectedActual
1Create an invoice from an order and complete the flow Invoice record createdAs expected
2Open the Invoices view and click the invoice row PDF loads in the viewer Persistent spinner; “Error downloading invoice. Please try again.”
3Open the same invoice via Edit or Send instead — PDF renders correctly — the document exists and is reachable this way
4Click Send with valid recipients populated Invoice emailed to the customer “Unable to send invoice” with a RETRY option

The view failure’s underlying request:

GET /api/v3/invoices/32a37a04-c24d-449a-b6dd-6b5bb7f489b0/pdf
404 Not Found

Logged from Invoices.service.ts:43 via getInvoicePdf → Invoices.tsx:996 → handleViewInvoiceOpen. Because the same document renders through Edit and Send, the PDF exists — the view path specifically is broken.

The send failure is a server-side rejection, not a transport error:

POST /api/v3/invoices/01c0fce1-6acc-4a30-8578-093f3ccd4f6f/send
400 Bad Request

Logged from Invoices.service.ts:106 via sendInvoice → EditInvoice.tsx:2008 → handleOnSend. Reproduced on Invoice #16, a routine $479.00 invoice with complete addresses and no unusual data. The offered RETRY is misleading: resubmitting an identical rejected payload will fail identically.

Business impact

Together these mean an invoice can be created but not delivered. Brokers and factoring companies require the invoice PDF, typically alongside a signed POD, before releasing payment — so an invoice that cannot be sent cannot be collected on. That is the entire purpose of the feature.

There is no workaround for the send failure. It occurs on a routine invoice with valid data, which means it affects every invoice rather than an edge case, and a carrier hitting it cannot bill their customer through the product at all.

The view failure has a technical workaround — the document renders through Edit — but not a discoverable one, and no user would find it. Functionally, an invoice that cannot be opened is an invoice that cannot be checked before it goes out.

Evidence

Recommended follow-up

Both failures are independent of the document itself, since the preview renders correctly. For the 404, compare the endpoint and parameters used by the view path against those used by Edit and Send. For the send failure, the 400 indicates the server rejected the payload — inspecting the response body would likely identify the offending field immediately. Separately, the client discards the server’s error detail and substitutes a generic message with a RETRY action, which is worse than surfacing the real reason.

Caveat

The environment was slow throughout the session, including one client-side ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE originating from my machine. Neither failure above is attributable to that: the 404 was consistent and reproducible across multiple invoices, and the send failure returns a server-issued 400 rather than a transport error.

Also affects download — confirmed during automation

The same defect blocks the download path. Opening Invoices → row menu → View invoice does open the viewer chrome — its download, print and close controls are present and reachable — but clicking download produces no file. Taken with the symptoms above, the invoice document itself is what cannot be produced or served; the surfaces that should display or deliver it all fail for the same reason.

Automated coverage for the download is written and ready — InvoicesView.downloadInvoice() asserts the saved file is a non-empty PDF. It is deliberately called by no test while this is open; wire it in once fixed and it will fail loudly on regression.

Finding 03

Linehaul rate is read-only when an order is edited from the orders list

Medium

Reproduction

StepExpectedActual
1From the Orders list, open the three-dot menu on any order Menu opensAs expected
2Select EditEdit screen opensAs expected
3Attempt to change the Linehaul rate Field is editable, as it is via other entry points Field is read-only, with no message or explanation
4Edit stops, scheduled dates, or stop types on the same screen —Editable, and the order saves normally
5Open the same order for editing via the order overlay —Rate is editable as expected

Business impact

The three-dot menu is the fastest route to editing from the orders list, and is likely a common path for a dispatcher correcting a load. A user who needs to fix a wrong rate finds the field locked with no explanation, and would reasonably conclude the order is locked because it has been invoiced — which is not the case. The likely outcomes are recreating the order unnecessarily, or leaving an incorrect rate in place and billing it.

A workaround exists — editing via the order overlay — which is why this is rated below the first two. But nothing on the locked field points to it, so a user who hits this has no reason to think another entry point would behave differently.

Recommended follow-up

The two entry points likely pass different props or fetch different data shapes into the same edit component. Worth checking whether other fields are affected on paths not tested, and whether the same flag also drives the invoice-status display.

Additional

Observations outside the assigned workflow

Not counted as findings

Document upload is non-functional application-wide

The Upload dialog reports “Document types are still loading. Please try again in a moment,” and the Upload button remains disabled. Not investigated as a primary area, since attachments fall outside the assigned scope — but it directly affects the billing outcome. Invoice packets typically require a signed POD, so this could block collection even when the invoice itself generates correctly. It is a contributing factor in my release recommendation.

Order margin displays inconsistently across views

For Order #14, the margin showed 100% on the create form, 0% in the order overlay, and - in the orders list — the same underlying data rendered three ways.

Investigated and ruled out: apparent disagreement between the two map providers

The route map plotted a stop in Austin, Texas, while the stop's hyperlink opened Google Maps at a location in North Charleston, South Carolina — roughly 1,100 miles apart. On investigation this traced to the underlying location record, which is stored as “HQ, 1 Seed Street” with no city or state. Google flags the result as a partial match and resolves the bare street name arbitrarily. To confirm, I created stops with complete addresses — 1600 Pennsylvania Ave NW, Washington DC and 2200 W Commerce St, Dallas TX — and both resolved correctly through the same hyperlink, which places the cause in the record rather than in the link-building logic.

I am recording this rather than reporting it as a defect: the behaviour is a consequence of incomplete seed data, not of the mapping integration. The two providers are also expected to differ on routing, since truck-legal routing and general navigation are not the same problem. The one point worth passing on is that address completeness does not appear to be validated when a location record is created, which is what allowed the misleading link in the first place.

Stop type can be left blank when editing

Editing an order from the orders list showed Stop 2 with an empty Type dropdown — neither Pickup nor Delivery selected. Not investigated further for time reasons, but a stop with no type is a data integrity concern worth confirming.

An invoice send hung indefinitely

One send attempt produced a persistent spinner with no error and no completion. The environment was slow throughout, so I could not separate application behaviour from environment behaviour, and I am not reporting it as a defect. It may share a cause with Finding 2.

Expired MUI X Pro license renders in the application UI

The watermark “MUI X Expired license key” appears in the Expenses panel and elsewhere, visible to users rather than only in the console. A licensing matter rather than a defect, but not appropriate for a release candidate. Visible in several figures above.

Console errors during invoice creation

A DOM nesting violation is logged from PreviewInvoice.tsx and CreateInvoice.tsx, alongside React key warnings in the location selector. Not user-visible, but the invoice path is not error-free, and the noise made the Finding 2 network error easy to miss.

Environment note

The application is served as a Vite development build — unminified sources and node_modules/.vite/deps paths are visible in stack traces. Some behaviour, particularly error handling and timing-sensitive interactions, may differ in a production build. The environment was also consistently slow, which shaped what I was able to investigate.
